issues.failure_explanation: In step (iv) of the proof of Theorem 4.3, equation (4.13) equates the sum over ordered tuples of LN-trees to a sum over LN-trees in \widetilde{\T}(r) with an inserted factor of N_P(\Upsilon). Because the tuples already uniquely parameterize the elements of \widetilde{\T}(r), introducing N_P(\Upsilon) overcounts terms possessing repeated branches. Consequently, when grouping equivalent LN-trees by equivalence classes in step (i), the resulting combinatorial prefactors \frac{\alpha(\Upsilon) S(\Upsilon)}{\gamma(\Upsilon)} in (4.5) are incorrect. For example, for the tree \Upsilon = [[\;]_0 [\;]_0]_0, the Taylor expansion gives a coefficient of 1/2 for A_j^m(\Upsilon) F_{t_{n, j}}^\Upsilon, whereas the formula yields \frac{\alpha(\Upsilon) S(\Upsilon)}{\gamma(\Upsilon)} = \frac{1 \times 2}{2} = 1.

failure_location.quote: R^{n, j} = \sum_{\Upsilon \in \T_r}  rac{\alpha r{\Upsilon} S r{\Upsilon}}{\gamma r{\Upsilon}} A_j^m r{\Upsilon}  r{\Delta t_n}^{\abs{\Upsilon}} F_{t_{n, j}}^{\Upsilon} + \mO r{ r{\Delta t}^{r+1}}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the combinatorial counting in equation (4.13) by removing the spurious N_P(\Upsilon) factor and adjusting the tree-based combinatorial factors in Theorem 4.3 so that they accurately reflect the multinomial coefficients of the multivariate Taylor expansion.
issues.overall_effect: The formula for the expansion coefficients in Theorem 4.3 is quantitatively incorrect for trees with repeated branches. However, because each term in the expansion remains proportional to A_j^m(\Upsilon), the condition A_0^m(\Upsilon) = 0 still guarantees that the corresponding local truncation error terms vanish, so downstream consistency (Theorem 4.4) and convergence results remain valid.
issues.title: Incorrect combinatorial coefficients in local error expansion
issues.why_classification: A routine correction of the combinatorial prefactors restores the validity of the expansion in Theorem 4.3 without requiring new lemmas, without changing the elementary coefficients A_j^m(\Upsilon) or order conditions C(r), and without altering any consistency, stability, or convergence results.
